entities.summary: Michael Stryphnos was a high-ranking Byzantine official under the Angeloi emperors, serving as the magister sacorum (master of sacred rites) from 1180 to 1201. He played a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the empire during a tumultuous period, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Angeloi, the Latin Empire, and the Seljuk Turks. Through his diplomatic efforts, Stryphnos helped to secure a temporary peace treaty with the Seljuks in 1198, allowing the empire to focus on internal reforms. His legacy extends to the development of the Byzantine liturgy, as he oversaw the codification of the Angeloi's liturgical practices and the creation of a standardized liturgical text. Stryphnos's influence can be seen in the subsequent reforms of the Byzantine church, which continued to shape the empire's spiritual landscape. Despite his significant contributions, Stryphnos remains a relatively obscure figure, overshadowed by the more prominent figures of his era. His story serves as a testament to the often-overlooked behind-the-scenes work of Byzantine officials, who played a vital role in shaping the empire's destiny.
